key_facts.fact: Sukhm Kang is an Exa FDE calling from the SF office, about 2 to 3 months in; his previous FDE-titled job was 'more of like infra engineer' and Exa is his first sales-involved role.
Sukhm named no customers and no verticals; he gave a hedged figure of 'maybe around 5000' enterprise customers and 'maybe 10 or 11' FDEs (transcribed as FTEs).

FDE vs AE split per Sukhm: the AE handles contracting and the relationship; the FDE is 'the main technical point of contact'; FDEs are 'heavily involved in the pre-sales, especially in the technical evaluations' and help customers tune the queries they send to Exa.

Sukhm tied competitive technical evaluations to AJ's resume ('similar to what you mentioned on your resume'); the Sales_Engineering resume summary opens 'Sales engineer who wins technical evaluations'.

The benchmark post AJ praised on the call is 'Introducing Exa Agent Ultra - A New Frontier for Deep Research' (Sep 25, 2026). It compares against Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra and Perplexity, and lists finance use cases incl. market mapping for due diligence, KYC compliance research, company enrichment and portfolio monitoring. Sukhm said many people worked on it.

Jenna's demo brief asks AJ to 'walk through everything you'd plan to show to the customer' and gives '~30 minutes to walk us through your customer framing, the live Exa demo, and the business impact'; the exercise is capped at 4 hours.

On the call AJ said 'almost 3 years' in trading tech, 'primary analyst for 5 clients', a CRD 'rotation of over 200 clients', and told the Adroit to HedgeServ drop-copy integration story: FIX spec 'over 50%' larger, delivered 'a month ahead'. He did not tell the trading-pipeline story.
Exa has two applications from AJ to the same posting: 8/28 (Forward_Deployed_AI resume) and 9/20 (Sales_Engineering resume); the intro invite came from the 9/20 one.
The 8/28 Why-Exa essay contains two now-wrong facts: 'the last two years building an ML trading system' and 'three years' at Charles River.
The 9/20 essays centre on the Adroit pre-go-live harness that lists every unmapped value, and on 'Finding the failure nobody has noticed yet'.
The Sales_Engineering resume Exa holds claims 17 data feeds and 1,028 tests for AJ-Algo-Trader; the prep script says several dozen feeds and about 970 tests.

71.4% means the pod's closed FIX L1 case count rose 231 to 396 (2023 to 2024) after AJ joined the queue; his personal share was 226 of 396 (57%), about 4x his three teammates' average, and this is interview-only.
The Adroit FIX spec revisions were Adroit revising its own spec to expand the product, not HedgeServ changing; the HedgeServ integration reached client UAT (not go-live) ahead of schedule.

Canonical facts: CRD two and a half years; just under three years of trading tech; MS in progress, class of 2027; trading system is paper-trading, never production; five CRD clients; Adroit full-time, Integration Specialist.
AJ's weak spot is invisible process (jumps to the cause silently, declines long stories, asks no questions back); on the same day at Alpha FMC he could not answer GET vs POST vs PUT.

The Exa search endpoint is POST https://api.exa.ai/search with 'x-api-key' or 'Authorization: Bearer' auth; parameters include query, type, numResults, category, includeDomains, excludeDomains, startPublishedDate, endPublishedDate, contents.

On AJ's machine: Python 3.11.9 with streamlit 1.59.1, pandas, plotly, requests, httpx, anthropic SDK, google-genai, python-pptx. exa_py, fastapi and flask are not installed. Node 24.18 plus a global n8n CLI are present; Docker is absent; R 4.6.0 is installed but not on PATH.
No Exa API key was found in the checked .env files; AJ-Algo-Trader/.env holds Alpaca, Gemini and Marketaux keys only (no Anthropic key).

Deloitte work (2021-2022) was researching private investment assets for SEC/PCAOB independence conflicts and running independence audits: an entity-research pain point that matches Exa's published KYC and company-enrichment use cases.

uncertainties: The call transcript is auto-transcribed and garbled (HedgeServ appears as 'Tetcher', FDEs as 'FTEs', Exa Agent Ultra as 'ex-Asian ultra'); Sukhm's '5000 customers / 10 or 11 FDEs' figures were hedged by him and may be mis-transcribed.

I could not prove which resume file Exa received on 8/28: the likely candidate is the Somerville-header build (which says HedgeServ 'production go-live', '>1000% reduction', 'Apr 2026 - Present'), but a Cambridge-header 'LLM Applications in Capital Markets' build also existed that day.
The 8/28 'proud of' and 'what motivates you' essays were not saved verbatim; only the application-log summary exists.

Several claims on the resume Exa holds have no confirmation record in memory: the $225M Tradeweb FIX tag discrepancy, '10+ leading institutional clients', '30+ releases', Readystate, 'Five years ... Fortune-500 clients', the retrieval-backed knowledge-base assistant. AJ should confirm them before repeating any.

The 'rotation of over 200 clients' at CRD and the 'a month ahead' HedgeServ timing appear only in AJ's spoken words on the call; an earlier resume session had dropped the one-month version as unconfirmed.
The Exa Agent Ultra benchmark numbers came through a summarizing fetch tool; re-read https://exa.ai/blog/exa-agent-ultra directly before quoting any percentage.
Ryan Ahern's title and whether he has read either resume or the essays are unknown; Sukhm gave no information about this round.
The prep doc's Glassdoor description of Exa's process (second call plus take-home, then a trial workday) was not verified by me; Jenna's email only describes this 30-minute demo round.
n8n's global CLI binary exists, but I did not verify that it starts or that any workflow is running; Lovable credits were exhausted as of 9/16 per memory.
The Providence Investment Management summers (AJ's claim of 'best performing in 08 and 09') have unconfirmed years and duties.
